fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

The rotation script was called on a fixed schedule (e.g. hourly). If it missed a scheduled run there was no recovery mechanism — the missed run was simply lost.

## What changed

Added a `_is_run_due(files)` helper in `rotation_script/rotation_script.py` that checks the modification time of the most recently written run file. If fewer than 3300 seconds (55 minutes) have elapsed since the last run, the script prints a skip message and returns early without doing any work.

This makes the script safe to call frequently (e.g. every 5 minutes via cron). When the scheduler fires more often than once per hour, the script is a no-op until a full interval has elapsed — so a missed run will be caught on the next firing without duplicate runs being written.

Three unit tests were added for `_is_run_due`: no-files case (always due), recent-file case (skip), and old-file case (proceed).

## How it was validated

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit rotation_script` — 8 tests passed (5 pre-existing + 3 new)

## Reviewer notes

The external scheduler (cron/systemd timer) should be updated separately to invoke the script every 5 minutes instead of every hour; that configuration lives outside this repo. The 3300-second threshold is exposed as `RUN_INTERVAL_SECONDS` at module level for easy adjustment.

Fixes #7488
